text:
alex: quick heads-up — traffic shape shifted this week. median tokens/request went from ~120 to ~290 across the board, and streaming calls are now ~45% of requests (was ~18%). this is starting to bite latency and cost.

maria: ugh. do we have a breakdown by model/region? is this concentrated or global?

alex: mostly us-west and eu-west. smallest signal in ap-south. 70% of the long-context calls are to the chat-v2 family (context > 8k). sample: median seq len on chat-v2-prod: 9.4k, p95: 18k.

sam: that explains the KV cache churn. hit rate dropped from 0.82 to 0.46 on the long-context pool. throughput per GPU is ~30% lower for these sessions.

jin: can you paste the perf counters? want to see GPU util / batch sizes.

alex: sure — quick top-of-pod snapshot from last 10m:
```
pod: longpool-3
gpu_util: 78%
avg_batch_size: 2.1
kv_cache_hit: 0.46
tokens/s: 420
latency_p50: 160ms
latency_p95: 1.9s
```

maria: tokens/s down and p95 ~2s is going to trigger a bunch of client retries. cost blowup incoming.

sam: do we know the incremental GPU hours estimate if this mix holds? need to feed finance and sales.

alex: back-of-envelope: current baseline for stable mix = 480 GPU hrs/day. with +2.4x median seq and 45% streaming heavy, we need ~620 GPU hrs/day to hit the same latency SLOs — so ~140 extra GPU hrs/day (~980 extra GPU hrs/week). if we partially mitigate with batching improvements maybe cut to ~600/day.

maria: 980 GPU hrs/week is material. at committed pricing that’s ~$XXk/week — finance will want options: routing, prewarm, or reserved long-context pool.

jin: mitigation ideas:
- route long-context to dedicated long-context pool (higher memory, wider kv slots)
- enable prefix-only cache for common system prompts to improve hit rate
- reduce client-side streaming chunk size (trade latency for throughput)
- opportunistic quantization for long-context variants

sam: timeline for dedicated pool? how fast can we carve / spin up a new reserved slab in us-west?

alex: we can provision a dedicated long-context slab (8xA100-style equivalents) in ~36h if we approve reserved capacity. prewarm + canary into it in 48–72h. autoscale cold-starts are too slow for this delta.

maria: can we try a quick routing rule to keep small chats on standard pool and heavy ones to current best-effort long nodes? low-risk A/B.

alex: yes — we can add a routing rule based on estimated initial token count (header hints). quick rule patch:
```
route:
  if initial_estimated_tokens > 250: send_to long-context-pool
  else: send_to standard-pool
```

ops-bot: deploy job queued: route-rules/quick-long-context -> staging (ci-4521). started by alex.

jin: if we do routing only, we still need capacity for the long-context bucket. estimate for a minimal reserved slab: 40 GPUs (8 pods x 5 GPUs equiv) to keep p95 < 2s for current load. that's ~160 GPU hrs/day.

sam: what about caching tweaks? prefix-only cache sounds promising and lower-cost.

alex: prefix cache for system prompts gives us +0.18 hit rate in sim; combined with increasing max batch window from 25ms -> 75ms yields an effective tokens/s uplift of ~22% in sim. tradeoff: a bit more jitter on tail latency.

maria: pinging finance: @maria can we get an estimate $/week for the 40 GPU reserved slab vs on-demand excess? also need to factor inter-region egress if we route to eu-west long-pool.

sam: also note network: some eu-west nodes are hitting NIC queues when sequences spike; if we push long-context to eu-west we should check MTU and peer link utilization.

jin: I'll run a quick NIC check and a simulated replay for the new route tonight. if NIC QDISC is saturated, we might need a smaller batch size + more pods.

alex: request: approve a short-term reserved capacity purchase for us-west 40-GPU slab for 2 weeks while we evaluate routing + caching. estimated cost delta: ~$28k/week. can we fast-track?

maria: approve provisional spend up to $35k/week for 2 weeks to avoid client-impact; finance: please confirm, ops will add tag long-context-experiment.

ops-bot: tag applied: long-context-experiment

sam: for rollout plan: 1) staging route rules + sim replay (today) 2) provision 40-GPU slab (after approval) 3) canary 2% of traffic to slab + metrics gating 4) expand to 25% if kv hit improves and p95 < 1.5s

jin: sounds good. I'll post PR for routing rule and run the replay. alex, can you draft the telemetry dashboard updates (kv hit, tokens/request distribution, reserved utilization)?

alex: on it — will drop charts and a one-pager in #eng-infra-runbooks. patch ETA 3h.

maria: thanks. quick reminder — include per-customer cost attribution so CS/sales can flag high-burden tenants.

alex: will do. also adding a short-term mitigation flag: if cost/latency escalate, we auto-block anonymous free-tier streams > 10k tokens until canary stabilizes.

sam: OK. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
